stories.title: RBI launches three surveys on inflation expectations and consumer confidence ahead of December meeting
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced the launch of three separate surveys to gather information on households’ inflation expectations and overall consumer confidence. The surveys are being carried out before the RBI’s policy meeting slated for December, providing the central bank with fresh data on price outlooks and sentiment.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
stories.summary: In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.previousTitle: RBI eases forex reporting rules for service exports and imports
stories.previousSummary: The Reserve Bank of India on Tuesday announced that, effective 1 October 2026, foreign‑exchange reporting requirements for service‑related exports and imports are being relaxed. Transactions up to Rs 10 lakh are exempt from filing a separate Export Declaration Form, and for resident individuals the form is deemed submitted once the authorised dealer bank receives the payment‑credit information, with no value threshold for them.

stories.title: Global Market Today: Asian shares retreat as US futures slide on Midterm election bets
stories.summary: Contracts for the S&P 500 Index dropped 0.3%, erasing an initial gain of 0.5%, while those for the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.6%. The dollar dropped against most of its Group-of-10 peers and the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note fell four basis points to 4.92%.

stories.title: Weak monsoon hampers winter sowing, raising food inflation concerns in India
stories.summary: Indian farmers are struggling to sow winter crops because a weak monsoon has left water supplies low, and Amarsingh Gushinge’s village reports a significant rainfall deficit. The shortfall threatens planting decisions and could push food inflation higher as staple prices rise, adding financial pressure on households. The Reserve Bank of India may consider interest‑rate hikes to curb the inflationary pressure.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.
